fixes.problem: street_sgt: the scanned Camry meshes were swapped for kit cars (parked.js line 36, buildCarModel simple=true). The near red sedan and the cropped blue car are flat extruded side profiles with no wheel arches, slab sides, a 1980s box silhouette and plastic paint. Parked cars also keep their headlights lit: the light material has emissiveIntensity 0.3 (vehicles.js line 38), so the red car's lamps read 237,224,211 at 18:15. The two nearest objects in the shot now look like a 2005 game. This is the biggest visual regression of the round.
fixes.fix: Hybrid LOD in parked.js. On the high/ultra tier, slots within 45 m of any views.json camera or the player spawn use the Tripo mesh (buildCarModel(kind, col, M, false)), instanced per kind with InstancedMesh.setColorAt for paint. Every other slot, and all of the low tier, keeps the kit car. Kit car upgrade in vehicles.js: subtract wheel-arch notches from K.prof (an arc of radius wr+0.05 at x = +-wb/2), add a shoulder crease at y 0.80 (scale z by 1.02 in a 0.04 m band), raise the beltline so glass height is 0.38 rather than 0.44 m, and lower paint metalness 0.45 -> 0.25 and roughness 0.22 -> 0.32 so the sky env stops painting the bodies blue-grey. Parked cars: a separate lightParked material with emissiveIntensity 0.3*uNight (0 by day).

fixes.problem: The de-clump worked, but the crowd starved: hero 8 -> 4, hero_noon 7 -> 4, phone_hud 5 -> 1 walkers. The cause is S.topUp (peds.js line 92). Candidates are still the raw LOOPS.eq/landing waypoints, all on one line 6 m inset at 14 m steps. With free() rejecting anything within 3.5 m of another walker, each band runs out of candidates (if (!cand.length) break) before it reaches its quota. The promenade now reads empty instead of lived-in (bible triage: 'people and traffic everywhere').
fixes.fix: peds.js S.topUp: build point candidates around each in-view waypoint. Offsets are 2.5, 6 and 10 m along the local shore normal (perpendicular of w[i+1]-w[i-1]) times -4, 0 and +4 m along the tangent: 9 points per waypoint. Keep free(), the bench rejection and the bands, but raise the quotas to [8-20:3, 20-35:3, 35-55:4] on high and [8-20:2, 20-35:2, 35-55:2] on low. On low, also reject candidates that project to screen x > 0.72 and y > 0.45 (under the right touch cluster). Snap each placed walker to the nearest loop index so pathing continues. Turn 2 of the high-tier walkers into idle pairs (gesture 'phone'/'look') standing 1.2 m apart, so the crowd has groups as well as walkers.

fixes.problem: hero inlet 109,110,115 (bible #2A566E = 42,86,110). The SEA_REFL distance blend landed but the near water still reads as a milky silver sheet with horizontal terrace bands, not water. At the 1.85 m eye height every near pixel is grazing, so Fresnel alone returns the sky. The normals are too smooth to break it up. At noon the same water goes pale pool-blue (hero_noon mid 109,138,158), close to the 'cyan swimming-pool water' avoid item. The bridge_skyline basin also lifted, 67,73,81 -> 86,96,108.
fixes.fix: sea.js: (1) Tint the reflection by the water body before mixing: pr *= mix(vec3(0.55, 0.78, 0.86), vec3(1.0), smoothstep(30.0, 250.0, d)). Real murky Swan River water absorbs red even in reflection at grazing angles. (2) Add a near-field micro-ripple octave to seaN: wavelength 0.5-0.9 m, amplitude 0.10, faded by smoothstep(60.0, 15.0, d). This gives dark/light ripple facets instead of terraces. (3) seaRough near 0.04 -> 0.07 so the sky blurs. (4) In daycycle at el > 40, envIntensity on the sea 1.0 -> 0.75 and scatter x1.2, so noon water is deep blue, not pale cyan.

fixes.fix: facade.js far branch: far glass is already mix(1.0, 0.55, far) (line 154). Also scale the far frame/spandrel albedo by 0.55 and raise far roughness to 0.30, so the blocks stop mirroring the bright horizon. atmos: cap aerial in-scatter on geometry to 0.55 of the sky horizon colour at 3-6 km (mix toward uHorizon by at most 0.55). The towers then keep a 15-20 luma gap below the sky.
